page: Microsoft Azure D64lds_v6 is a compute-focused general purpose virtual machine powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor running up to 4.2 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture and deployed via Microsoft Hyper-V, the instance allocates 64 dedicated vCPUs across 32 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The CPU subsystem is equipped with a large 260 MB L3 cache alongside advanced vector and matrix acceleration instructions, including AVX-512 and Intel AMX. The instance pairs this high compute density with 128 GB of system memory, yielding a 2 GB per vCPU ratio, and includes 3,780 GB of direct-attached local NVMe SSD storage without integrated GPUs.

Benchmark results highlight strong throughput across core computational and data-handling workloads. The server achieves a PassMark CPU score of 70,905.37 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 20,508.0, with top-tier marks in image processing and static web serving throughput reaching 97.56 GB/sec. Memory read operations in cached blocks deliver 4,425.91 GB/sec, while uncached reads sustain 254.01 GB/sec. Benefiting from AMX extensions, LLM prompt processing reaches 39.92 tokens per second on large 70B models, while PassMark database operations and Redis SET throughput record strong top-quartile performance.

From an architectural efficiency standpoint, the reduced memory allocation relative to standard general purpose tiers prioritizes compute cycles and fast local I/O over massive in-memory pools. This resource profile prevents paying for unneeded memory capacity when hosting high-concurrency workloads. The primary tradeoff lies in memory-intensive processing, where 2 GB per core may constrain large databases entirely reliant on memory retention. Consequently, Microsoft Azure D64lds_v6 is ideally configured for scale-out web serving, compilation pipelines, batch media processing, caching layers, and database deployments leveraging fast local NVMe storage.
description: Microsoft Azure D64lds_v6 is a virtual machine featuring 64 dedicated vCPUs across 32 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8573C processor capable of reaching 4.2 GHz. Supported by 260 MB of L3 cache, Intel AMX, and AVX-512 instructions, the server balances processing speed with 128 GB of memory and a bundled 3,780 GB NVMe SSD for fast local storage. Benchmark results validate strong multi-core computation, exceptional static web serving throughput of 97.56 GB/sec, and efficient small-model and large-model prompt processing. With a 2 GB per vCPU memory footprint, it offers high resource efficiency for workloads that demand substantial processor cycles and high-speed local disk without requiring memory-optimized capacity tiers. The configuration is well matched for high-traffic web hosting, CI/CD compilation, vector-accelerated batch operations, caching servers, and local-disk database engines.
